events.name: Swan Lake by International Ballet Stars
events.info: ONE NIGHT ONLY - A must-see theatrical event. Experience the world's most beloved ballet like never before. International Ballet Stars returns with a breathtaking production set to Tchaikovsky's iconic score and performed by a world-class international cast representing four continents. From the moonlit lakeside where Princess Odette is held under a powerful spell, to the dazzling royal ballroom where the seductive Odile delivers the legendary 32 fouettés - every scene is filled with drama, precision, and unforgettable beauty. This large-scale, immersive, Broadway-caliber production brings together over 150 handcrafted costumes, richly detailed sets, and an exceptional company of dancers to create a spectacular live experience. Elegant, emotional, and visually stunning, Swan Lake is more than a ballet - it is a night at the theater you will remember long after the final curtain. A timeless story of love, betrayal, and redemption, captivating audiences of all generations.

boxOfficeInfo.willCallDetail: The Will Call window is located at the front Box Office window. Tickets held at Will Call can be picked up early as 1 1/2 hours prior to show. Customer must present the actual credit card, photo I.D., and the confirmation number.

venues.parkingDetail: Parking is located along Palafox, parking garage on Jefferson (one block over).

generalInfo.generalRule: 1.) No smoking is permitted in theatre. 2.) No outside food or beverages are permitted in the theatre.
generalInfo.childRule: There are no age restrictions. Children under 2 are admitted free without seat. Child age for discounts is 2-12.

ada.adaCustomCopy:
To better accommodate your needs, Saenger Theatre has requested that all accessible seating ticket accommodations be solicited only through their representatives. Please contact a Saenger Theatre representative for further help with your ticket purchase.*   Advance ticket purchase may be required. 
 
* Box office information is subject to change.
